title: Rupee steady as oil firms buy dollars
description: The Indian rupee showed minimal movement against the dollar on Friday, closing nearly unchanged. Oil companies actively bought dollars to restrict any considerable appreciation of the rupee. State-run banks also contributed to dollar selling in the market. The rupee fluctuated within a narrow scope, revealing a slightly negative trend, while Brent crude oil prices stabilized around eighty-three to eighty-four dollars per barrel.

With geopolitical risks and rate-cut hopes providing further support, analysts see potential for gold to resume its long-term bull run.

title: FIIs now backing India's consumers, not capex: July data reveals major rotation

Consumer services, healthcare and consumer durables attracted Rs 25,298 crore, while capital goods, telecom and automobiles faced heavy selling. The shift highlights stronger preference for domestic consumption, healthcare and discretionary growth over capital expenditure-driven sectors.

The consolidated income jumped by 40%, reaching around Rs 20,753 crore. Notably, jewellery sales, excluding bullion, rose by 43% to Rs 18,253 crore, while the watches and EyeCare segments also saw significant revenue boosts.

description: Upcoming inflation data poses a challenge to the stock market's recent technology-driven surge. Analysts predict a rise in consumer prices, which might sway the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy. Meanwhile, easing geopolitical concerns and dipping oil prices have provided some reprieve to investors. Strong corporate earnings are exceeding forecasts, fostering a positive outlook for stocks, while fluctuations in yields and oil prices are being meticulously observed.

title: Ola Electric's Q1 revenue drops 45% YoY but loss narrows to Rs 336 crore

The company earned four hundred fifty-five crore rupees in the first quarter, with vehicle registrations also dropping as compared to the previous year. Despite this, Ola's net loss displayed a slight improvement, narrowing by about twenty-one point five percent year-on-year, with overall unit deliveries also decreasing.
